description: The IOS to Flutter Equalizer Bridge is a project that allows the Flutter application to communicate with the native IOS equalizer. This document will walk you through my thought process of creating the bridge and the challenges that were faced.

text: I am building a music player application in Flutter and wanted to integrate an equalizer. Flutter does not provide a built-in equalizer, and existing third-party plugins either lack multi-band support or do not support iOS. Because of this, the only viable approach was to create a custom bridge between Flutter and the native iOS equalizer. So that is what I did.
The main functions I wanted to include in the bridge were:

list: have a sick UI controller for the equalizer
have a way to save the settings
have a way to load the settings
have a way to reset the settings

text: The primary challenges I expected included audio latency, overall audio quality, UI implementation, rewriting portions of my app’s audio-handling logic, and the limited bridging support provided by Flutter. Audio latency was a major concern because the audio needed to be processed in real time. The UI was another obstacle since no existing libraries offered a design I could easily integrate, and I had never worked with Flutter’s CustomPainter before. I also anticipated difficulties with Flutter’s platform channel system since I had not used it previously.
